status: PRE-REGISTERED (primary verdict) plus one labelled secondary fairness check added after the primary result, to answer the obvious objection to the pre-registered scoring choice.
phase: Master plan sections 24-25 (model selection: the model must earn its complexity) and section 43 (do not confuse statistical significance with practical usefulness).
why_now: E012 compared the 1h move-size model against the BASE RATE and against chance. It has never been compared against a simple rule that adapts. 'How often has a large move happened lately?' is a direct empirical estimate of exactly the quantity the model predicts, it needs no fitting, no calibration, no walk-forward machinery and no artefact -- and if it matches the model, the model's nine inputs, its quarterly refits and its Platt calibration are buying nothing. This is the cheapest possible way to find out that the one positive result in the project is not worth its complexity, and it must be asked BEFORE any more complex model family is considered.
hypothesis: The fitted, calibrated nine-input logistic model predicts next-hour move size better than a simple trailing-frequency rule, by enough to be worth its complexity.

candidates.A_expanding_base_rate: P = share of all hours BEFORE this one whose |1h return| exceeded the threshold (a point-in-time prior; the trivial reference).
candidates.B_trailing_24h: P = share of the last 24 hours of completed one-hour returns whose |return| exceeded the threshold.
candidates.E_ewma_halflife_24h: exponentially weighted mean of the same 0/1 indicator, half-life 24 hours, computed causally.
candidates.F_one_feature_logistic: the simplest FITTED model: L2 logistic on tr_mean_14_rel alone, same walk-forward and Platt calibration as the incumbent (this is E018's k = 1 set).
candidates.G_incumbent: the frozen research deliverable: L2 logistic on all nine inputs with Platt calibration (E012 + E013), model_version move_size_1h_v1.

point_in_time_argument: The label for reference hour s is |close(s+1h)/close(s) - 1| > 0.0025, i.e. the size of the candle that OPENS at s+1h. At decision hour t the reference candle (opening at t) has closed, so every close up to and including close(t) is known, hence every label-return for s <= t-1. Rules B-E use a window of completed one-hour returns ending at the candle that opens at t, which is exactly those hours and no later one. Windows are measured in TIME, not in rows, so a data gap shortens the window instead of silently reaching further back -- the same rule scoring 0.2.0 now applies. Rule A uses only hours strictly before t.
method: Every candidate is scored on EXACTLY the rows the incumbent produces in its walk-forward (27 folds, 54,472 out-of-sample hours; 13,127 of them in validation), so the comparison is like-for-like. The non-fitted rules B-E are evaluated AS THEY ARE, uncalibrated: their appeal is that they need no fitting, and a simple rule that needs a calibrator fitted on a purged slice is no longer simple. Their ECE is reported so their honesty is visible. Uncertainty on every difference is a circular block bootstrap, blocks of 48 hours, 2000 resamples, seed 31, PAIRED on identical rows.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED. The incumbent EARNS ITS COMPLEXITY only if BOTH hold on the validation period: (i) PRACTICAL -- its skill (1 - Brier/Brier of the period base rate) is at least 1.10x the best simple rule's skill, i.e. at least 10% more skill; AND (ii) STATISTICAL -- the paired block-bootstrap 95% interval of (Brier of that best simple rule minus Brier of the incumbent) excludes zero. If (ii) holds but (i) fails, the recorded verdict is 'statistically better, practically equivalent -- the complexity is not earned'. Both parts are required because E018 showed that on 13,127 paired rows a paired test detects differences far too small to matter; the practical bar is what keeps that honest.
tripwire: If ANY simple rule beats the incumbent on validation Brier, that is investigated before being recorded -- it would mean either that the fitted model adds nothing over recent history, or that there is an implementation error. Investigation comes first, the result is reported either way.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: If the simple rules match the incumbent, the honest deliverable becomes a trailing-frequency estimate rather than a fitted model, Phase 12 should confirm THAT, and the whole E012/E013 apparatus is revealed as complexity without benefit. If the incumbent clears both bars, its complexity is justified and model-family research (section 24) can proceed from a defended starting point.
decision_this_experiment_may_not_make: It may not change scoring, may not change the live BUY/HOLD/SELL path, may not silently replace move_size_1h_v1, and may not touch the sealed holdout.

periods.validation: out-of-sample test blocks 2024-01-01 -> 2025-06-30 (the criterion is judged here)

target.outcome: close of the candle opening at as_of + 1h

verdict.statement: the fitted model earns its complexity

results:
THE FITTED MODEL CLEARS BOTH PRE-REGISTERED BARS, COMFORTABLY. On the 13,127 validation hours (no row dropped; every candidate had a value everywhere), validation skill is: expanding base rate -0.0094, trailing 720h +0.0098, trailing 168h +0.0210, trailing 24h +0.0321, EWMA half-life 24h +0.0398, one-feature logistic +0.0582, incumbent +0.0983. The best NON-FITTED rule is the 24-hour EWMA; the incumbent has 2.47x its skill (practical bar: 1.10x -- PASS) and the paired block-bootstrap interval on the Brier difference is +0.01459 [+0.01261, +0.01652], far from zero (statistical bar -- PASS). The tripwire did not fire: no simple rule beat the incumbent anywhere.

FAIRNESS CHECK (secondary, not pre-registered). The obvious objection is that the simple rules were scored uncalibrated while the incumbent carries Platt calibration, so the check was run: every simple rule was given the incumbent's exact advantage -- a Platt re-map fitted on the same purged 90-day slice of each fold, applied to the same test block. It helps them, and it does not change the answer. The 24-hour trailing rule improves most (ECE 0.056 -> 0.013, skill +0.0321 -> +0.0421) and becomes the best simple rule, but the incumbent is still 2.33x more skilful and both bars still pass. Two rules get WORSE when calibrated (expanding prior, trailing 720h), which is what a re-map fitted on 90 days does to a slow-moving rule in a changing regime.

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY SHOWS. Recent realised volatility is genuinely most of the signal -- a 24-hour EWMA of 'did the last hours move a lot?' already reaches 40% of the model's skill with no fitting at all -- but the model is not merely re-reading it. It more than doubles that skill, ranks better (rho +0.360 vs +0.235) and is better calibrated out of the box (ECE 0.014 vs 0.024). The exploration period tells the same story with bigger numbers throughout (incumbent +0.1457 vs best simple +0.1216), so this is not a one-period effect.
affected_design: The 1h move-size model's complexity is now DEFENDED, not assumed: it beats the honest non-fitted alternative by a factor of two on validation, before and after giving that alternative the same calibration. Nothing about any running system changed. Two consequences for later work: (1) model-family research (master plan section 24) may proceed from a defended starting point rather than from an unexamined one; (2) the EWMA rule is worth keeping as the standing reference in any future move-size experiment -- comparing to the base rate alone, as E012 did, sets the bar far too low, and every future move-size result should be reported against this rule as well.
